expects.query: Run the IN-1 runtime and API validation on the running deployment. First verify uploaded/stored video playback through VIOS by uploading an existing warehouse sample MP4. Then verify the live streaming half by using the NvStreamer validation source, registering its RTSP URL with VIOS, driving RT-VLM on the VIOS proxy URL, and proving streamed dense captions reach Kafka topic `mdx-vlm-captions` and Elasticsearch. Use API-discovered sensor IDs and RTSP URLs; do not construct them from assumptions.
checks: After VIOS upload, `GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` returns a JSON array containing a sensor whose name matches the uploaded video's filename stem, and `GET /sensor/<sensorId>/streams` returns a non-empty array.

After upload, `GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/stream/<streamId>/picture?startTime=2025-01-01T00:00:05.000Z` returns HTTP 200 with `content-type: image/*` and `size_download > 2000`, confirming uploaded video is retrievable for playback.

After upload, `GET http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/storage/file/<streamId>?startTime=2025-01-01T00:00:03.000Z&endTime=2025-01-01T00:00:05.000Z&container=mp4&disableAudio=true` returns HTTP 200 with `content-type: video/*`, `size_download > 1000`, and a valid MP4 body.
NvStreamer is reachable: `curl -sf --max-time 15 http://localhost:31000/vst/api/v1/sensor/version` returns exit 0 and reports `.type == "streamer"`, distinct from VIOS on port 30888.

The staged sample video is auto-discovered by NvStreamer: `GET http://localhost:31000/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` returns a JSON array containing a sensor whose `name` equals the staged sample filename stem.

The RTSP URL is read from the NvStreamer API, never constructed: resolve the sensorId from `GET http://localhost:31000/vst/api/v1/sensor/list` by matching `.name == <stem>`, then `GET .../sensor/<sensorId>/streams` returns a non-empty array whose `.[0].url` matches the NvStreamer RTSP pool.
The NvStreamer RTSP URL is registered with VIOS via `POST http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/add` with body `{"sensorUrl":"<url-from-streams-API>"}`; the response is HTTP 200 with a `sensorId`.

RT-VLM is driven on the VIOS live proxy URL `rtsp://${HOST_IP}:30554/live/<sensorId>` using `${HOST_IP}`, not `localhost`, through `POST http://localhost:8018/v1/streams/add` and `/v1/generate_captions` with `stream:true` and a non-empty prompt.

Within 120 s of stream registration, Kafka topic `mdx-vlm-captions` end offset advances over its pre-registration baseline, verified via `docker exec kafka kafka-get-offsets --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --topic mdx-vlm-captions`.

Within 120 s of stream registration, Elasticsearch contains caption documents, verified via `curl -sf 'http://localhost:9200/_cat/indices?h=index,docs.count&v' | awk '$1 ~ /^default_/ && $2+0 > 0'` returning a non-empty result.
Elasticsearch caption documents follow the VSS 3.2 `<collection>_<id>` index naming shape, not the legacy `mdx-vlm-*` or `mdx-vlm-1970-01-01` pattern.
The final runtime check distinguishes the uploaded/VOD playback path from the live streaming caption path and reports evidence for both.
No upstream compose file was modified during runtime validation (`git diff --quiet HEAD -- deploy/docker/` returns exit 0 at the end of the run).
